html:
Kunya-Urgench, old Urgench, in northern Turkmenistan, was the capital of Khwarazm, the oasis of the lower Amu Darya. Its ruins hold a tall minaret and royal tombs, mostly from the 12th to 14th centuries.

As Gurganj it was the capital of the Khwarazmian Empire until the Mongols broke the dams and flooded it in 1221. It rose again under the Golden Horde, when the Kutlug Timur minaret, about 60 metres high, and the tomb of Turabek Khanum were built.

Timur sacked it in 1388, and when the Amu Darya changed its course in the 16th century the city lost its water and was left. Khiva took its place. The site is a World Heritage Site and a place of pilgrimage for Turkmen, who visit the tomb of the Sufi Najm al-Din Kubra.
